_about: The Find my fit quiz's own values per platform (the rest of its scoring comes from the published answers and cards). Served next to the page and loaded with the code's ?v= number, so score.js and these values always arrive together: run build\bump-version.ps1 after editing this file. ease: how easy it is to run without technical skills (0 needs a developer, 3 easiest). look: the design control it suits (template, visual = arrange pages yourself, pixel = every detail). lookBest: for an exact tie between two platforms, the one whose card's first tag is about the design control asked for wins it (Wix's drag-and-drop editor for arranging it yourself, Squarespace's designer templates for a template); only where a card says so, and the tag must be on the card. largeCatalogue / smallShop / b2b: stores it suits (b2b: profiles that name selling to other businesses). storeOnly: only for selling. agency: a common choice for designers and agencies, only where the card's "Good fit" lines name designers or agencies (Duda, WordPress, Webflow's "Teams with a designer", Framer's "Designers coming from Figma"); agencyOnly: mostly sold through them. customFrontEnd: built to feed an app or any front end. devControl: built to be coded. members: newsletters to paying members sent by the platform itself (Ghost), a bonus on top of the published "Sell memberships or paid posts" row. bookings: bookings or appointments from the platform itself or its own first-party product, for "Anything you'll need from day one?" → Bookings: Wix (Wix Bookings), Squarespace (Squarespace Scheduling, the Acuity product it owns, sold as an add-on plan), HubSpot (its meetings scheduler), Square Online (Square Appointments, Square's own, as a booking page). Everywhere else bookings come from a third-party app or plugin, which the result says as "worth knowing". imports: for "Moving from somewhere?", what each platform's own docs say it imports from another platform on the picker: imports[destination][origin] = { what: the content as the docs list it, url: the docs page }. Only the platform's own documentation counts (BigCommerce's are its own Data Migration app pages; WordPress's are WordPress.com's importers, which read the same files self-hosted WordPress imports through Tools → Import). Framer's WordPress and Webflow guides describe rebuilding, not importing, so they're not listed; Duda's URL import copies text and images into its content library from any address, not a platform's content, so it isn't either. The result shows the match's line as a reason with the docs link, no points. Checked 2026-10-31. notIdeal: a card's "Less suited if" lines that clearly match a quiz answer. "if" is the start of the line as it reads on the card (the persona test and every publish check it's still there); "when" is the matching answers (all keys, any listed value). A match rules the platform out unless nothing else fits; the rule reads only the answers, never the card text. Lines with no clear matching answer stay plain text, including Ghost's "several languages" (its languages answer already counts against it). Drupal's "It’s a small site, or there’s no developer" rules it out for someone building it themselves and for local businesses and portfolios, which are small sites. WordPress’s "no maintenance" applies only to a custom build by someone not technical who wants the platform to host it; elsewhere managed hosting covers it, and the hosting question already counts against it. fitFor: a card's "Good fit" lines that answer a quiz question. A line tagged with a kind of business is what makes a platform suit that answer to "Which is closest to what you do?" (3 points), so a platform suits only the kinds its own card names; every tagged line also breaks an exact tie: "line" is the line as it reads on the card (the persona test checks it's still there), "when" the answers it answers (all keys, any listed value; a line that answers two different questions is listed twice). When two platforms score the same, the one with more matching lines comes first and the result says why; with the same count they stay tied. WordPress's "Custom sites and apps that draw on its content (its REST API)" (added 2026-11-01) rests on its REST API handbook, https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/ (a new front end, or its content in separate applications). Only lines that plainly name what the person is making (its kind, a store's size, a publication, a custom build) are tagged, never who builds it or how it's hosted. domainDocs: the platform's own help page for connecting a domain (official docs only; none where the developer's host does it), linked from the first steps on a result. Checked 2026-10-31. managedHosting: platforms whose published hosting line names a managed option that takes updates and security on, so wanting hosting handled counts -2 instead of -6, or +2 when an agency or developer builds the site, as they arrange the managed host (the score's "managed" part): WordPress (managed WordPress hosting and WordPress.com handle updates and security), Magento 2 (Adobe, on Adobe Commerce Cloud). freeDomain: platforms whose free plan publishes only to their own address, so your own domain needs a paid plan, with that address and the platform's own page saying so; a result that starts free on one says it as "worth knowing", no points. HubSpot is left out: its own pages disagree on whether the free tools connect a domain. "needs" words what your own domain takes when it isn't a paid plan (Substack: a one-time fee). Checked 2026-11-01. revenueShare: platforms that keep a share of what paid members pay, which the monthly cost bands don't show, with the platform's own page saying so; a result for paid members on one says it as "worth knowing", no points (Substack: its cost answer, checked 2026-11-01). Substack and Square Online (added 2026-11-01): Square Online's card names shops, cafés and restaurants already using Square, not local businesses in general, so its line isn't tagged; it reaches them through selling and bookings, which the quiz scores already. HubSpot's "You don’t otherwise use HubSpot" rules it out for every business site and publication unless "We already pay for HubSpot" is ticked (a tick on "Which is closest to what you do?"; in "when", a tick that isn't given reads as "no"); ticked, HubSpot gets 4 points, as its card's first "Good fit" line is businesses already using HubSpot's CRM or marketing tools (3, as for a kind, moved the agreed "B2B marketing team on HubSpot" persona to Webflow).
